publicRelease: 1.0.5 was published from 88f8808ee66c6de733d718bd7588f96677a9da47; a version number cannot be reused, so the contract fixes shipped as 1.0.6 and then as 1.0.7, which registry.npmjs.org serves as latest with gitHead 0209e8e176e5b0fc36f6b9bd3c1fa49476370af0 and shasum 603c5fc76c5512483b0a68f3e06fb4787bb50eb4, its tarball byte-identical to npm pack at that commit

manifestCompatibilityFix.change: manifest-only: engines.dsh and dsh.compatibility.dsh moved from a single version or a 0.1.7-rc.1 floor to the range ">=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.2.0", dsh.compatibility.node added ">=22.19.0", and dshReleases plus dshOperations now declare every release in the live latest-three window: 0.1.7-alpha.2, 0.1.7-rc.1 and 0.1.7-rc.2
manifestCompatibilityFix.windowAuthority: official-dsh-releases.mjs resolves the latest-three window from official GitHub Releases and published npm versions in the active major.minor line; previews tagged on the next channel that belong to a later major.minor line are deliberately excluded
manifestCompatibilityFix.runtimeEvidenceCarriesForward: for 1.0.7 itself: lib/index.js and client/client.js were byte-identical to 1.0.6, so the end-to-end evidence in the matrix above applies to that release unchanged
manifestCompatibilityFix.undeclared: a release that has not been tested stays undeclared rather than being claimed, so it reads as unknown; peer dependencies still pin 0.1.7-rc.1
manifestCompatibilityFix.method: each release ran against its own @deepseek-ai/dsh CLI in a throwaway DSH_HOME: profile 'acceptance' built from the shipped web template, dsh-worktree-space-1.0.7.tgz installed, --dump-config composed the worktree-space row, cold start printed its URL with no warning, the page carried dsh-worktree-space/client.js with the plugin RPC answering ok:true, then remove dropped the package and left zero occurrences, and a second cold start was clean

observations.pnpmPeerNotice: the routine '[WARN] Issues with peer dependencies found' appears in every install, including the already-verified 0.1.7-rc.2; it is not a version incompatibility

archiveStrategyRelease.change: the archived-documents root became a configured strategy instead of one computed rule: dsh.compatibility.dshOperations is untouched, but the finish dialog now chooses between the task space's own container root (<container>/archived-docs, the new default) and a configured directory, and files documents under <project>/<task>-<stamp> beneath whichever root is in force rather than a flat <workspace>-<stamp> folder
archiveStrategyRelease.hostContractUnchanged: the Host side of the archive is the same surface: task.done still carries the same documentsDirectory string, finishTask still validates it with assertIsolated against the task container, and archive.js's copy/clean-up paths are unchanged. The Host plugin gains one configuration field and one accessor, and lib/index.js is rebuilt for it.
archiveStrategyRelease.clientBundleChanged: client/client.js is no longer byte-identical to 1.0.6 or 1.0.7 - it now computes the destination from the served strategy - so the byte-identity claim recorded under manifestCompatibilityFix stops at 1.0.7
archiveStrategyRelease.lifecycleRowsNotReRun: not yet run for 1.0.8: the install/start/uninstall/rollback rows in the matrix above were taken against 1.0.6 and 1.0.7 tarballs and have not been repeated against a published 1.0.8. The two roots are covered by unit tests (test/documents.test.ts) and by the finish-dialog tests (test/task-finish.test.tsx) only so far; the disposable-profile matrix should be re-run before 1.0.8 is offered to the Catalog
archiveStrategyRelease.dumpConfigCountsMayMove: the --dump-config line counts recorded above are 1.0.7's; a release that adds a configuration field may compose a different tree, so those numbers must not be carried into a 1.0.8 claim without measuring again

projectLayerRelease.change: a task space moved down one level: it was <container root>/<task>/<repository> and is now <container root>/<project>/<task>/<repository>, with the project layer named after the source Workspace directory (basename of the source root) and derived by the plugin rather than asked for. The recommended container root is unchanged - 'worktree-space' inside the first directory below the volume root - so source roots of one root workspace share a single container however deep their own project is filed, and the container strategy's archive root is that container root itself, so every project shares one archived-docs rather than one per project.
projectLayerRelease.containerRootValidation: the container root is now the plugin's zone: the first task space created under it writes a bilingual README.md (an existing one is never overwritten), and a container root that is itself a git repository - it holds a .git - is refused before any directory is created. That refusal covers the case where the container root is the source repository itself, which assertIsolated already rejected from the other side.
projectLayerRelease.protocolGainedACoordinate: task.plan and task.done now take a required project alongside task and tasksRoot, createTask's result and every task's metadata carry it, the task_worktree_space tool gained the parameter and a two-level list, and the client's TaskGroup, types and create/finish payloads follow. This is a breaking change for this plugin's own client half, not for any external service.
projectLayerRelease.oldLayoutNotMigrated: the flat <container root>/<task>/ layout is neither supported nor migrated: listTasks walks two levels below the container root and skips archived-docs, and a task space created by an earlier version will not be listed.
projectLayerRelease.evidenceAndDumpCountsInvalidated: the end-to-end row in the matrix above was taken at 1.0.6 with the flat layout, so its paths are one level short and it is evidence for neither the project layer nor the 1.0.8 archive strategies. lib/index.js and client/client.js are rebuilt again for this change, and the --dump-config line counts remain 1.0.7's.
projectLayerRelease.lifecycleRowsNotReRun: not yet run for 1.0.8: the project layer, the container-root README and the .git refusal are covered by unit tests (test/task-operations.test.mjs, test/task-paths.test.mjs, test/task-naming.test.mjs, test/task-tool.test.mjs) only. The disposable-profile matrix should be re-run - and should now exercise the two container-root validations - before 1.0.8 is offered to the Catalog.

tasksRootStrategyRelease.change: where a new task space goes became a configured strategy beside the archive's: a 'Task space location' setting picks between 'default' - the derived recommendation, unchanged - and 'custom', which reads a 'Custom task space root' directory. Both are new Host configuration fields, and empty under the custom strategy still derives the recommendation, so a profile that never touches them behaves exactly as 1.0.7 did.
tasksRootStrategyRelease.oneResolutionPoint: resolveTasksRoot(sourceRoot, requestedRoot, configuredRoot) gained the third answer, and task.suggest-root, task.create and the task_worktree_space tool's suggest-root/create all call it, so the dialog's prefilled root, the root a create lands in and the root the model proposes are one value rather than three. A caller that names a root - the dialog's field, the tool's tasksRoot - still wins: this is a default, not an enforcement, and assertIsolated judges a configured root by the same rule as a typed one.
tasksRootStrategyRelease.strategyGatesTheDirectory: configuredTasksRoot answers with the directory only while the strategy is 'custom'; a directory left over from an earlier custom run goes inert the moment the strategy returns to the default. The create dialog writes the pair in that order - directory first, strategy second - so a refused directory is never paired with a strategy that reads it, and a refused strategy leaves only an inert directory behind.
tasksRootStrategyRelease.noProtocolChange: unlike the project layer, this changes no request or response shape: tasksRoot stays the field it was and only the meaning of its emptiness is extended, so this plugin's own client half is not broken by it. The client bundle changes again for the two rows and the create dialog's checkbox, so its byte identity stops at 1.0.7.
tasksRootStrategyRelease.copyCorrections: wording only, no behaviour: the store listing's experimental sentence, the agent-handoff entry's description, and the archive location's default wording. The create dialog's checkbox carries the same sentence as the setting it writes. The plugin description itself was rewritten in the same pass - it now leads with the task, says every repository gets a worktree on a branch of the same name and the task space is registered as an agent Workspace, and closes on merging back to the main branch and deleting the branches and the task space. That sentence lives in three places that must move together: locale/zh.json and locale/en.json (meta.description, the beta tail kept verbatim), package.json's description, and the client's panelDescription - the last of which is in client/client.js, so the client bundle changes again this round. Documentation paths were also rewritten from drive-letter backslash examples to `~/` with forward slashes across both READMEs, SKILL.md and both store-evidence files; that notation change reaches no code.
tasksRootStrategyRelease.lifecycleRowsNotReRun: not yet run for 1.0.8: the accessor and the suggest-root endpoint are covered by test/host.test.mjs, the resolution fallbacks and the isolation refusal by test/task-operations.test.mjs, the tool by test/task-tool.test.mjs, and the settings card's two rows plus the create dialog's checkbox and its two writes by test/plugin-config-card.test.tsx and test/create-flow.test.tsx - unit tests only, no runtime evidence. Four configuration fields were added across 1.0.8, so the --dump-config line counts recorded above are 1.0.7's and must be measured again.
